name: A Key to Netherworld's Secrets
take: Both Reincarnate follow-ups — Movement of Fate and Finality and Murmurs in a Haunting Dream — gain 80% to their multipliers, and idling out of combat with a near-empty staff auto-writes Cadenza notes until she holds two. Her warm-up disappears: the composition is already started before the fight is.

name: A Rope Tied to a Life Beyond
take: Scarlet Coda gains 75%, its per-Aftersound scaling gains another 75%, and casting it refunds 14 stacks of Aftersound on the spot. The crescendo pays for its own next performance — the Coda loop stops having a cooldown in any sense that matters.

name: A Dagger to Cut Clean Obsessions
take: Echo Skill DMG amplified by 80% — which is Hecate's entire off-field output in one line. Scarlet Coda also converts the whole staff to Cadenza notes, and Cadenza hits cut the target's ATK by 20%. Offense and a defensive debuff in the same stroke, which is the most Fractsidus sentence imaginable.

name: A Torch Illuminating the Path
take: Every Echo Skill cast hands ALL Resonators 20% Attribute DMG Bonus for 30s. She casts Echo Skills constantly by design, so this is effectively a permanent team-wide damage aura wearing a chain node's clothes.

name: A Forked Road in Fate's Heartland
take: Entering Maestro drops a 4s Stagnation field — the room holds still for the overture — and she takes 30% reduced damage for the whole state. The conductor's podium gains a moat.

name: A Night to Depart From Eternal Rest
take: Enhanced Hecate attacks gain 24%, the Reincarnate follow-ups now command Apparition of Beyond — a bonus 216% Hecate strike that refunds 8 Aftersound on hit — and the finale splits by position: off-field, targets take 40% more from them both; on-field, she gains 60% Havoc DMG. Either answer is correct. That's the point of a duet.
